The top horizontal straight line through the three top circles has arrow product 30. Label the top row left-to-right as A, B, C; the middle row left-to-right as D, E; and the bottom row left-to-right as F, G, H. From the diagram, the straight arrow lines are A·B·C = 30, B·D·F = 48, C·E·G = 105, A·D·G = 28, and B·E·H = 144. Now reason: The numbers 1 through 8 are used once each. The product 28 can only be made by the distinct triple {1,4,7}. The product 105 can only be made by {3,5,7}. The product 144 can only be made by {3,6,8}. Since E lies on both the 105-line and the 144-line, E must be the common number in {3,5,7} and {3,6,8}, so E = 3. Therefore on the 144-line, B and H are {6,8}; on the 105-line, C and G are {5,7}. Using the top product A·B·C = 30, with B in {6,8} and C in {5,7}, the only possibility is B = 6 and C = 5, giving A = 1. Then G = 7. From A·D·G = 28, we get 1·D·7 = 28, so D = 4. From B·D·F = 48, we get 6·4·F = 48, so F = 2. Finally H = 8. The bottom row is F, G, H = 2, 7, 8, whose sum is 17.
